In a PR of @Yaël Dillies #38714, it causes the following example to experience a slowdown by ten times:

import Mathlib

variable {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [CommGroup G] [Fintype G] (g : G)

open Representation CategoryTheory

set_option trace.profiler.useHeartbeats true in
set_option trace.profiler true in
example (hg : ∀ x, x ∈ Subgroup.zpowers g⁻¹) {i : ℕ} :
    @ModuleCat.of k _ (A.ρ.tprod (Representation.leftRegular k G)).Coinvariants
    (Coinvariants.instAddCommGroup (A.ρ.tprod (Representation.leftRegular k G)))
    (Coinvariants.instModule (A.ρ.tprod (Representation.leftRegular k G))) =
    @HomologicalComplex.X ℕ (ModuleCat k) (ModuleCat.moduleCategory k)
    Preadditive.preadditiveHasZeroMorphisms
    (ComplexShape.down ℕ) (HomologicalComplex.coinvariantsTensorObj A
    (Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex) i := by
  rfl

the heartbeats taken in master branch is 2539519 and the heartbeats taken in yaels PR is 23795363, I don't quite understand it and could use some help, maybe @Kevin Buzzard you're interested in this kind of things? :)
I could look but right now I'm stuck on a beach with no laptop. Normal service will be resumed next week

The heart of the matter seems to be that on master we have things like

[] [825.000000] ✅️ Coinvariants.instAddCommGroup
      (A.ρ.tprod
        (leftRegular k
          G)) =?= Coinvariants.instAddCommGroup
      (((MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor (Rep.{u, u, u} k G)).obj A).obj
          ((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i)).ρ ▶

and these are very quickly checked to be defeq, whereas on the branch we have things like

[] [7000722.000000] ✅️ Coinvariants.instAddCommGroup
      (A.ρ.tprod
        (leftRegular k
          G)) =?= Coinvariants.instAddCommGroup
      (((MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor (Rep.{u, u, u} k G)).obj A).obj
          ((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i)).ρ ▶

(looks the same, takes 10000 times as long because everything gets unfolded). So what has happened is that something has changed very slightly (e.g. it looks like there are two routes from CommRing to Semiring and now for some reason we're taking another one) and so two terms which used to be syntactically equal are now very slightly different and this causes some nightmare unfolding to begin. I will look more later but that's at least a start.

This code

import Mathlib

variable {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [CommGroup G] [Fintype G] (g : G)

open Representation CategoryTheory

variable (A : Rep.{u, u, u} k G) (hg : ∀ x, x ∈ Subgroup.zpowers g⁻¹) {i : ℕ}

example : Representation k G
    (TensorProduct k (↑A)
      (G →₀
        k)) = Representation k G
    ↑(((MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor (Rep.{u, u, u} k G)).obj A).obj
        ((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i)) := rfl

works on master but fails on the branch. With pp.all true the two (huge) terms are identical on master and the branch (if I got it right)

I think the answer is that the defeq check

example : leftRegular k G = ((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i).ρ := rfl
/-
master
[Elab.command] [715642.000000] ✅️ example
  [definition.header] [381667.000000] ✅️ _example ▶
  [definition.value] [78114.000000] ✅️ _example ▶

branch
[Elab.command] [2616564.000000] ✅️ example
  [definition.header] [2254261.000000] ✅️ _example ▶
  [definition.value] [106662.000000] ✅️ _example ▶
-/

is much quicker on master than on the branch. This causes some things to unfold quite a lot and the problems multiply, e.g.

example : A.ρ.tprod
    (leftRegular k
      G) = (((MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor (Rep.{u, u, u} k G)).obj A).obj
      ((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i)).ρ := rfl
/-
master
[Elab.command] [1169416.000000] ✅️ example :
  [definition.header] [798713.000000] ✅️ _example ▶
  [definition.value] [135476.000000] ✅️ _example ▶

branch
[Elab.command] [17723305.000000] ✅️ example :
  [definition.header] [10462392.000000] ✅️ _example ▶
  [definition.value] [7025988.000000] ✅️ _example ▶
-/

(note that on the branch those numbers are 10x as large) is a term which shows up in the original code and is far more painful on the branch.
Aha, in the PR I change the definition of the left-regular representation from Finsupp to MonoidAlgebra. This must be related
docs#Rep.leftRegular
(deleted)

I don't really understand properly why the slowdown occurs. The issue is something like the following: ((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i).ρ is, if you unravel it, just literally leftRegular k G, so you would imagine that Lean would just unfold Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution and it would all be over quickly. But unfortunately things aren't so simple. leftRegular k G has type Representation k G (MonoidAlgebra k G) and ((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i).ρ has type Representation k G ↑((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i), so now all of a sudden we need to check that these types are equal, and Lean has to solve

G →*
                MonoidAlgebra k G →ₗ[k]
                  MonoidAlgebra k
                    G =?= G →*
                ↑((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i) →ₗ[k]
                  ↑((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i)

(this is before even checking that the terms are equal -- we're checking that things typecheck). This opens up a real can of worms because now we have lots of things like

[147248.000000] ✅️ MonoidAlgebra.instModule =?= ((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i).hV2

to check and all of these are expensive, and they get more expensive on the branch.

I guess that this is an indication that there was some defeq abuse going on in the original question. It might be worth thinking about that.

Right so the original question is an attempt to prove that two objects in the category ModuleCat k are equal. An object of this category is a type, and an AddCommGroup instance on the type, and a Module k structure on the type. So Lean is faced with this question after unfolding:

[] [21059345.000000] ✅️ { carrier := (A.ρ.tprod (leftRegular k G)).Coinvariants,
      isAddCommGroup := Coinvariants.instAddCommGroup (A.ρ.tprod (leftRegular k G)),
      isModule :=
        Coinvariants.instModule
          (A.ρ.tprod
            (leftRegular k
              G)) } =?= {
      carrier :=
        (((MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor (Rep.{u, u, u} k G)).obj A).obj
              ((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i)).ρ.Coinvariants,
      isAddCommGroup :=
        Coinvariants.instAddCommGroup
          (((MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor (Rep.{u, u, u} k G)).obj A).obj
              ((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i)).ρ,
      isModule :=
        Coinvariants.instModule
          (((MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor (Rep.{u, u, u} k G)).obj A).obj
              ((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i)).ρ } ▼

All this is data, so we need to check that all fields are equal. The first fields (the types) are equal but the proof is painful, and so checking that the second and third fields (the group and module structures on the not-syntactically-equal types) are equal is also going to be painful. Note also that with_reducible rfl fails on the original question, and it also fails on the underlying types:

example : (A.ρ.tprod (leftRegular k G)).Coinvariants =
    (((MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor (Rep.{u, u, u} k G)).obj A).obj
              ((Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution k g⁻¹ hg).complex.X i)).ρ.Coinvariants := by
  with_reducible rfl -- fails

So I think it's not an unreasonable question to ask why you want to make these objects equal.

@Yaël Dillies Do you have any clue?

Thanks for minimizing! I've had a look at the slow trace, and I think the problem is the fact that #38714 defines some new instances by going through Equivs. In particular, we now have

instance : Module R S[M] := coeffEquiv.module _

where we used to have

instance : Module R S[M] := inferInstanceAs <| Module R (M →₀ S)

The instance created by inferInstanceAs is very efficient to unfold (similarly to what you'd get from fast_instance%). On the other hand, the new instance is slow to unfold, because Equiv.module and MonoidAlgebra.coeffEquiv both need to be unfolded.

We have seen similarly bad slowdowns around WithVal, whose instances were being declared using Equivs, which got somewhat improved using fast_instance%.

Hopefully it can be fixed with a simple fast_instance% on the Module instance!
good news : it drastically decreases heartbeats from 2236526 to 535058!
Are there any other instances in the PR which are defined through the equiv R[M] = (M ->_0 R) without usingfast_instance%?

Kevin Buzzard said:

Are there any other instances in the PR which are defined through the equiv R[M] = (M ->_0 R) without usingfast_instance%?

plenty, for example these instances in here

@[to_additive (dont_translate := N) isScalarTower]
instance isScalarTower [SMulZeroClass N R] [SMulZeroClass O R] [SMul N O] [IsScalarTower N O R] :
    IsScalarTower N O R[M] := coeffEquiv.isScalarTower ..

@[to_additive (dont_translate := N) smulCommClass]
instance smulCommClass [SMulZeroClass N R] [SMulZeroClass O R] [SMulCommClass N O R] :
    SMulCommClass N O R[M] := coeffEquiv.smulCommClass ..

@[to_additive (dont_translate := N) isCentralScalar]
instance isCentralScalar [SMulZeroClass N R] [SMulZeroClass Nᵐᵒᵖ R] [IsCentralScalar N R] :
    IsCentralScalar N R[M] := coeffEquiv.isCentralScalar _
Note that for Prop classes the value doesn't matter, so fast_instance% won't do anything there.

Do you mean that you think there are proofs that would break because they depend on unfolding these instances?

Are we talking about transferring an instance of Add along an equivalence and then making the transferred instance unexposed? My experience is that typeclass inference often wants to unfold these things to check defeqs
My hunch is that this abuse of defeq is now removed because MonoidAlgebra was made a one field structure instead of a def.

Are we talking about transferring an instance of Add along an equivalence and then making the transferred instance unexposed? My experience is that typeclass inference often wants to unfold these things to check defeqs. The situation I see is where you have two non-syntactically equal but defeq types both of which have got an add via such a transfer and then typeclass inference has to unfold everything including the definition of add just to check that they're the same

Kevin Buzzard said:

The situation I see is where you have two non-syntactically equal but defeq types

Exactly, thanks to Yaël Dillies's PR, the two types are not even defeq anymore, so we are not in this situation.

I have made a draft PR which no_exposes the definition of Add. There are a few awkward changes that need to be made - we'll see if it builds and if it gives a performance improvement.

It looks like there are a couple of places that rely on unfolding the Add instance (see #41362). @Yaël Dillies, do you think we should try to remove this defeq (ab)use, or can the definition of addition be considered part of the API of MonoidAlgebra?

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

Exactly, thanks to Yaël Dillies's PR, the two types are not even defeq anymore, so we are not in this situation.

I mean that you have defeq but not syntactically equal X and Y, and then you apply the equiv to both of them and now you get adds on both of them and have to check they're equal, and this involves unfolding the definition. I saw this in the context of WithVal at least.

If we do not want to remove the defeq entirely, we could also go for an intermediate option to make the instances for Add, Neg, etc. be semireducible. This was already previously the case because inferInstanceAs would wrap these parts of the instances because they were leaky. They are not leaky anymore, so we don't wrap them anymore, but it could be beneficial for performance.

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

It looks like there are a couple of places that rely on unfolding the Add instance (see #41362). Yaël Dillies, do you think we should try to remove this defeq (ab)use, or can the definition of addition be considered part of the API of MonoidAlgebra?

Mind explaning what one of these (ab)uses looks like?

You can have a look at the build failures in #41362. In particular some of them are a type mismatch where (x + y).coeff appears on one side and x.coeff + y.coeff appears on the other side. These expressions are not anymore definitionally equal if we don't expose the addition.
That looks like abuse to me, yes
I think we could go either way on this. Note that we can't hide the defeq for smul
